assertion.objects: A=Z2[[t]][1/2], a nonzero f in A and an A-module element killed by f.
assertion.hypotheses: Coefficient denominators are uniformly bounded; character specializations are compatible with the A-action and take values in characteristic-zero fields.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such f and module element, separately on each rational sign component.
assertion.parameter_range: Finite-order cyclotomic characters, including the trivial character separately.
assertion.uniformity: Only finitely many exceptional character values for each fixed f; no uniform count in f asserted.
assertion.constants: The coefficient-dependent epsilon and finite exceptional orders are not claimed uniform in the family.
assertion.normalizations: t=gamma-1, character value zeta-1; normalized v2(2)=1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The zero series is excluded. No arbitrary unbounded-denominator power series is allowed.
assertion.limit_order: Evaluate convergent power series at positive valuation; no exchange with cohomological inverse limits.
assertion.statement: If the actual retained Euler-system class in one rational sign component were torsion, its compatible cyclotomic specializations could be nonzero at only finitely many characters. The separately supplied reciprocity/nonvanishing inputs then exclude torsion.

use.reason: Apply the coefficient-minimum proof to an annihilator of the actual class. Specialization compatibility suffices; no cohomology base-change isomorphism is needed.
use.shared_contract_justification: One actual caller in the nonvanishing argument.

supplier.statement: A nonzero bounded-denominator power series has finitely many cyclotomic zeros; a module element killed by it specializes to zero away from those finitely many characters.
